_note: The progression spine: XP from every match and course run, an account level it fills, and three rolling challenges. Ours: Apex, Warzone and Fortnite all publish their XP tables only in part and change them every season, so these are shaped like theirs rather than copied. What they share, and what this keeps, is that you always earn something for playing, more for playing well, and the most for finishing a goal you were given.
_xp: XP a match pays. played is for finishing one at all. kill and damagePer100 reward the fight, win and roundWon the result. A battle royale pays for placement instead of rounds: brTop3 and brTop10 are placement bonuses (a placement counts as top 10 only in a lobby bigger than 10), and brPerMinute pays for survival, capped at brMinutesCap so a match spent hiding cannot farm it. A course run pays courseRun, plus the medal's bonus.
_levels: Level n to n + 1 needs first x growth^(n - 1) XP, rounded to 50. An ordinary match (finished, two kills, 300 damage) pays about 300 XP, so at 1,500 and 1.04 the first level is about five matches and level 50 about seven hundred, which is roughly a long season's pace. cap is where it stops counting up.
_challenges: The pool the three active challenges are drawn from, in order: a finished one is replaced by the next one in the pool that is not already active, so they rotate rather than repeat. stat names what counts: kills, damage, hits and wins from any match; br for a battle royale played, brTop3 for a top-three finish, arena for a mode match (Gun Run, team deathmatch, free-for-all, Crown, Control), runs for a course run finished.
